listening.title: Listening 1 — New Media at School
listening.passage:
Teacher: How does your class use new media for school projects?
Maha: We use a class platform to share ideas and documents. We also use video calls when a group member is absent.
Teacher: How do you decide whether online information is reliable?
Maha: First, I check the source. I look for the author and the date, and I compare important information with another reliable website.
Teacher: What about screen time?
Maha: I try not to use my phone late at night because it can affect my sleep. During study time, I turn off unnecessary notifications.
Teacher: Do you think social media is useful?
Maha: Yes, if we use it responsibly. It helps us communicate quickly, but we should protect our privacy and think before posting.
Teacher: What is your most important rule?
Maha: I never share private information or a photograph of someone without permission.

listening.title: Listening 1 — Climate Change
listening.passage:
Presenter: Today we are talking about climate change and what students can do to help.
Salim: What is one major cause of climate change?
Presenter: Burning fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas produces greenhouse gases. These gases trap heat in the atmosphere.
Salim: What effects can climate change have?
Presenter: It can increase temperatures and contribute to droughts, floods and rising sea levels. Some communities may also face problems with water and food supplies.
Salim: Can students make a difference?
Presenter: Yes. They can save electricity, reduce waste, reuse items and recycle materials. Walking or using public transport when possible can also reduce emissions.
Salim: Is one action enough?
Presenter: One small action may seem limited, but millions of responsible actions can make a difference. Schools can also plant trees and teach students about sustainable choices.
Salim: What is the main message?
Presenter: We cannot solve climate change through one person or one day. We need long-term action from individuals, communities and governments.

listening.title: Listening 1 — Renewable Energy in Oman
listening.passage:
Engineer: Why is renewable energy important for Oman?
Student: Oman has many sunny days, so solar power has strong potential. Some areas are also suitable for wind power.
Engineer: How do solar panels help?
Student: They use sunlight to generate electricity. Wind turbines use moving air to generate electricity.
Engineer: Are renewable sources completely without challenges?
Student: No. Large projects need investment, suitable technology and careful planning. Engineers also have to consider the location and how electricity will be supplied to people.
Engineer: What are the main advantages?
Student: Renewable energy can reduce the use of fossil fuels and lower some emissions. It can also support a more sustainable future.
Engineer: What should students remember?
Student: Renewable energy is not only about solar panels. It is about choosing cleaner energy sources and using energy efficiently.
Engineer: Can Oman benefit from these projects?
Student: Yes. With good planning and investment, renewable energy can support Oman’s future energy needs.

listening.title: Listening 1 — Oman and Civilisation
listening.passage:
Guide: Today we are visiting a site that helps us understand Oman’s history.
Student: What kind of evidence do historians use?
Guide: They study archaeological sites, buildings, objects and written records. These sources help them understand how people lived in the past.
Student: Why were trade and seafaring important?
Guide: Oman had connections with different regions through trade and the sea. Merchants travelled and exchanged goods and ideas.
Student: What is heritage?
Guide: Heritage includes important cultural and historical traditions, places and objects that communities want to preserve.
Student: Why should young people care about it?
Guide: Heritage helps people understand their identity and history. It also allows future generations to learn from the past.
Student: How can students help?
Guide: They can respect historical places, learn about local history and share accurate information. They should never damage archaeological sites or remove objects.
Student: So preserving heritage is also a responsibility?
Guide: Exactly. Protecting the past helps communities build a better understanding of the future.
